title: MaRAV6 controls plant architecture by repressing brassinosteroid biosynthesis in banana
content:
Abstract
The substantial height and dense foliar overlap in banana plants critically constrain light interception and utilization. Optimizing petiole inclination to achieve a compact plant architecture is therefore crucial for enabling high-density cultivation and facilitating mechanized harvesting. However, the underlying genetic and molecular regulatory mechanisms remain largely unknown, owing to banana genome complexity and clonal propagation. In this study, we utilized a panel of 143 accessions exhibiting significant variation in petiole inclination to dissect the genetic architecture through genome-wide association studies (GWAS). This analysis identified 42 significant single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) and 389 candidate genes. By integrating transcriptomic data from the conventional cultivar “Baxi” and its dwarf and erect petiole mutant “R3,” we prioritized MaRAV6, an ABI3/VP1-related transcription factor-encoding gene located on chromosome 4, as a key candidate. Functional validation demonstrated that overexpression of MaRAV6 confers a dwarf and erect growth phenotype in banana. Combining DNA affinity purification sequencing (DAP-seq) and RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) further revealed that MaRAV6 represses the expression of brassinosteroid (BR) biosynthetic genes, steroid 22α-hydroxylase (MaDWF4-1) and brassinosteroid-6-oxidase (MaBR6ox1-1). This study elucidates first a molecular framework governing petiole angle regulation in banana. It also provides essential genetic resources and molecular targets for breeding compact banana varieties to enhance planting density and harvesting efficiency.
